build_quiz.description: Build a whole multi-round quiz in one step and get back a numbered question sheet and a matching answer key. Open Trivia DB takes one category per request, which is exactly the shape a quiz is not, so this makes one request per round and numbers the result end to end. Pass a session token and no question repeats between the rounds. No API key required.

parameters.description: Optional. One category per round, in the order they should be asked; leave it empty for a single round of mixed questions. This is the thing the API itself cannot do: it takes one category per call, so a five-round quiz is five calls, and they are made here. Give the name or the id: 18 and "Science: Computers" are the same category, and so is "computers", because the "Entertainment: " and "Science: " prefixes half of them carry are ignored. Capitals, accents and punctuation do not matter. Open Trivia DB allows one request every 5 seconds, so a five-round quiz takes about twenty seconds to build. Up to 10 rounds in one step.
parameters.name: categories

parameters.description: Optional. How many questions to ask in each round. Between 1 and 50, which is the service's own per-request limit; 5 by default.
parameters.name: questions_per_round

parameters.description: Optional. Leave it empty to mix all three. Narrowing this is the commonest reason a request finds nothing: there are far fewer hard questions than easy ones in most categories, and Get a category's question count says how many.
parameters.name: difficulty

parameters.description: Optional. Leave it empty for both. Multiple choice questions come back with four options; true/false with two, always in that order.
parameters.name: question_type

parameters.description: Optional. A token from Start a session token. While it is used, Open Trivia DB never hands the same question back twice, which is what a daily quiz needs. Leave it empty and repeats are possible. A token is dropped after 6 hours of inactivity.
parameters.name: token

parameters.description: Optional. Changes the order the options are shuffled into. By default the order is derived from the question itself, so the same question always lays out the same way and a reply graded later is graded against the letters that were sent. Set this only when you want a different, still repeatable, order.
parameters.name: seed

check_answer.description: Mark somebody's answer against the right one, however they wrote it. A quiz that goes out by email or chat comes back as "b", "B.", "microsoft" or "yes", and a plain comparison marks every one of those wrong. This resolves a letter or an option number against the options the question came with, compares text without regard to case, accents or punctuation, and accepts the words people actually answer a true/false question with. Makes no request, so it is not rate limited.
check_answer.name: check_answer

parameters.description: Optional, but pass it whenever the question was multiple choice: the answers list from the question step. Without it a reply of "B" is only text, and cannot be read as the second option.

create_session_token.description: Start a session token, which is how a recurring quiz avoids asking the same question twice. Pass the token to every question step and Open Trivia DB will not hand back a question it has already given that token. Tokens are dropped after six hours of inactivity, and once a token has seen every question matching a query it needs resetting. No API key required.

mock_response.note: Pass this token to every trivia step that should not repeat itself.

get_category_count.description: Find out how many questions one category holds, split into easy, medium and hard. This is what to check before asking for a large or narrow batch: a request for more questions than exist fails outright rather than returning what there is, and there are far fewer hard questions than easy ones in most categories. No API key required.

The question, its lettered options and the right answer are all ready to use: send question text as it stands, and keep the correct letter to mark the reply against. No API key required.

get_questions.description: Get up to 50 trivia questions from the Open Trivia Database, narrowed by category, difficulty and type. Every field comes back as plain text rather than the encoded form the API returns, and every question arrives with its right and wrong answers already merged, shuffled and lettered A to D, so a message can be built from it without any further work. A numbered question sheet and its answer key come back alongside. No API key required.

list_categories.description: List every category in the Open Trivia Database with its id and name, and optionally how many questions each one holds. The counts come from the one endpoint that reports them all at once rather than from asking each category in turn, which at this service's rate limit would take two minutes. Use it to build a category picker, or to choose a category at random for a daily quiz. No API key required.
list_categories.name: list_categories

reset_session_token.description: Wipe a session token's memory so every question is available to it again. This is the fix for a question step that starts failing because its token has already handed out everything matching the query - a narrow daily quiz will get there - and it keeps the same token rather than needing a new one threaded through the workflow. No API key required.

mock_response.note: The token has forgotten every question it has handed out.

message.description: What the service said about it.

previous_token.description: The token that was sent to be reset.

token.description: The token to keep using. Normally the same one, but use whatever comes back here.
